newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Coconut Bank shaves pricing.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Coconut Bank shaves pricing.

text.p: United Coconut Planters Bank shaved a couple of basis points off the most recent pricing for similar Philippine banks with its new issue launched on Thursday.
Other new FRCD issues were in the market as well.
United Coconut Planters Bank launched via arranger BA Asia a US$100 million two-tranche FRCD.
The three-year certificates pay a margin of 75 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 85 basis points to top tier managers.
The five-year paper pays a margin of 85 basis points and an all-in return of 94 basis points after fees.

The pricing is quite a bit tighter than Coconut Bank's three-year FRCD launched last July, which paid 100 basis points all-in. But the margin is close to the 87 basis points Rizal Commercial Bank paid last October.
Bankers said the Coconut deal, albeit just a few basis points tighter than Rizal's most recent FRCD, sets a new benchmark for Philippine bank issues.

"Coconut is setting a new benchmark because it is the first time a Philippine bank issue has been so tight," said a syndicate manager in Singapore, adding "and Philippine pricing is likely to get even tighter."

Coconut Bank's FRCD is the second Philippine bank dollar FRCD launched this year. Solidbank, which is about half the size of Coconut Bank in terms of total assets, launched a three-year deal on January 3 that paid an all-in of 92.5 basis points.
Indonesia's Bank Niaga set a US$40 million FRCD through joint bookrunners Bayerische Landesbank Singapore and Sumitomo Finance Asia.
The certificates have a five-year final maturity and puts and calls in years three and four.

They pay a coupon of 70 basis points over LIBOR for the first three years. Thereafter, if the options are not exercised, the issue pays 50 basis points over LIBOR in year four and in year five. The all-in is 87 basis points to the first put.
The bank's prior issue, a five-year FRCD with puts and calls in years three and four that was launched in September 1996, paid 92 basis points all-in.
Countrywide Corp, acting through its Hong Kong branch, set a US$100 million FRCD that pays an all-in return of 11 basis points over LIBOR.
The issue is guaranteed by Countrywide Banking Corp, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank of Scotland.
In other news, Thai Farmers Bank raised its doubtful loans provision for the first quarter of 1997 to 1.050 billion baht (US$40.38 million) compared with 486 million baht in first-quarter 1996.
A bank spokeswoman said the move reflected the bank's view that Thailand's economy will worsen this year.
